packs.title: Fossils, Fish and Open Sky
packs.promise: Follow curious objects, campus water and park paths across three city outings.

q.s: Make two fossils tell different stories.
st: Enter with applicable admission and choose two fossils or fossil displays currently on view.
Use their labels to note a difference in body shape, scale or the way each animal lived.
Give each display a two-word nickname of your own, then explain which observed detail earned it.

q.s: Turn an open park into a pocket design.
st: Choose a dry public path position and spot three different outlines in the park.
Simplify each into a line, curve or block on paper or in a note.
Arrange the three into a small emblem and name it after something you observed today.
From open visitor paths, find two contrasting edges: perhaps water and vegetation, grass and path, or open sky and trees.
Describe each edge with two texture words, without touching plants or approaching wildlife.
Choose which edge you would draw first and give one observed reason.

packs.title: Main Street in Detail
packs.promise: Read old facades, browse new ideas and collect small discoveries on two connected afternoons.

st: Choose three textures visible from a public path: one built, one growing and one on the ground.
Describe each without touching or collecting it.
Rank the three from most regular to most irregular and explain your first choice.

q.s: Let a gallery pair start a conversation.
st: In an open public gallery or lobby exhibit, choose two works currently on view.
Note a label reference for each and compare one use of color, line or material.
Write one question that the two works make you want to ask, using your own words rather than copying the artist’s text.

q.s: Turn a reading stop into your own question.
st: Choose an available book or public display that catches your curiosity.
Note its title/author or display reference and read a short available section.
Write your own one-sentence question inspired by it, then give your question a three-word title. Do not copy a passage.
